chunks: Does he give you a promise that when you are dead and turned to dust and bones, you will be raised to life again?
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic argument for resurrection after bodies turn to dust and bones?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Mu'minun (23:35) captures the core Shia theological debate on *al-Ba'th al-Jismani* (bodily resurrection), where skeptics argue that the decay of bones into dust makes physical reassembly impossible. It serves as a rhetorical challenge to divine omnipotence, asserting that the Creator who initiated existence can easily restore it, a concept reinforced by the Imam Ali's interpretation of this verse as a refutation of materialist nihilism. The emphasis on 'dust and bones' underscores the tangible reality of the afterlife, countering spiritualist views that might deny physical resurrection.
